title: Increasing Adoption Leave from 12 Weeks to 16 Weeks
what_it_is: Increasing Adoption Leave from 12 Weeks to 16 Weeks

sections.label: Maternity leave and adoptive parents
sections.summary: Maternity leave is a month longer as biological mothers need more physical recovery, while adoptive parents get the same parental and childcare leave benefits as biological parents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The duration of maternity leave is longer, by a month, as biological mothers require more time to recuperate physically from childbirth.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Adoptive parents, otherwise, receive the same parental and childcare leave benefits as biological parents today.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This includes the new 10-week Shared Parental Leave scheme, which was introduced last year to encourage shared parental responsibility and provide more time for parents to care for and bond with their newborns.

sections.label: Considering leave duration by need
sections.summary: Leave duration is considered by need, with a difference between those who give birth and those who adopt, and the key consideration is what is required.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In considering the duration of leave, we will look at the need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this case, as I have explained, there is a difference between those who give birth physically to a child and those who adopt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are not closed to considering fresh ideas or initiatives, but I think the key consideration must always be what is the need and what we want to support, and what is actually required.
